_note: Curated categories the sensitivity check looks for. It flags for human review; it never certifies an ad as safe.
global: Religious imagery, places of worship or sacred figures placed next to a product, used as a sales prop, or shown disrespectfully
Religious festivals or mourning observances used for selling in a way that trivialises them
Race, ethnicity, caste or tribe: stereotypes, jokes, colourism or 'fairness as aspiration', and casting that tokenises
Regional, language or national rivalries; mocking accents or dialects
Political parties, leaders, flags, protest movements or slogans; anything that reads as taking a side in a live political issue
National symbols (flags, anthems, emblems, maps) used commercially or altered; this can also be illegal
Food taboos tied to religion or culture (e.g. beef, pork, alcohol, non-vegetarian food in vegetarian settings)
Body shaming, disability as a joke, mental health trivialised
Gender stereotypes, and in rights campaigns anything that blames victims, sensationalises violence, or shows identifiable survivors
Children in unsafe situations or adult themes; advertising unhealthy food or toys directly to young children
Misinformation about health, law or rights; promises a campaign cannot keep
Firearms, drugs, alcohol or gambling where the audience or law makes them inappropriate

India: Caste references and surnames as markers
Beef in Hindu or Jain contexts, pork in Muslim contexts
United States: Race and policing, immigration and border politics
Partisan politics in an election cycle
United Kingdom: Class stereotypes and regional accents as jokes
The monarchy, national flags and football rivalries

Chennai: Temple imagery is especially sensitive next to products
Kolkata: Durga Puja idols and pandals near products
Bengaluru: Kannada language pride; local vs migrant framing
Lucknow: Hindu–Muslim framing; Awadhi culture shown as only Muslim or only Hindu
Atlanta: Black culture used as aesthetic without Black voices
Miami: Latin American communities flattened into one culture
Glasgow: Scottish identity treated as English; Old Firm football sectarianism
rural: Condescension toward rural people; showing rural women only as victims; land and caste issues; local dialect mocked
